notes:
Topline: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing code-assistant and cross-product semantic search. Strong emphasis on predictable throughput and per-tenant isolation. POC underway to validate latency SLOs at 99th pct and model-quality after aggressive quantization.

Summary of requirements (customer):
- Workloads: low-latency interactive code completions (avg target p95 <= 80ms), embedding generation for search (throughput spikes, batch windows), reranking for result pages (high QPS).
- Throughput/Capacity: expect baseline 500 concurrent sessions for code-assistant, bursts to 1.5k QPS for embeddings during index refreshes. Looking for reserved GPU pools sized to guarantee steady-state throughput with defined burst capacity.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets defined by product team: 20/80/200 ms for short-context completions; eager about Redwood routing policies to maintain SLOs across model variants and regions.
- Cost sensitivity: constrained budget vs self-hosted (internal infra). Wants clear unit-economics and options to trade cost <-> latency (e.g., batching windows, KV caching).
- Models: primary preference for Llama-3-like open models and a smaller proprietary dense LLM for code tasks. Want test on both fp16 and 8-bit quantized variants.
- Security/compliance: must run inside customer VPC for PII traces; KMS-based key management; SOC2 + ISO27001 proof required.

POC activities to date (timeline):
- 2024-09-20: Intro call — AE (Priya) + SE (Marco) + engineering leads. Captured throughput targets and security constraints. Drive links created.
- 2024-10-02: Security RFI submitted; Redwood provided baseline SOC2 artifacts. Jira SEC-209 opened for deeper crypto/KMS questions.
- 2024-10-18: Initial Dedicated sizing workshop — estimated 8x A100-equivalent for baseline steady state, + 3x for burst headroom. Notes saved in drive SOW draft.
- 2024-10-29: Fireflies meeting ff_0148721 — demo of batching + KV cache shows 27% token-cost reduction for search workload; Helmstone asked for model-specific quantization accuracy numbers.
- 2024-11-01: Engineering sync — validated p95 latency for code-assistant on fp16 model; 8-bit quantized model introduced 2-3% drop on unit tests in edge cases (token completion for rare code patterns). Ticket INF-872 created to gate quantization profile options.

Model-specific tuning notes (requested by Helmstone):
- Context length: primary code-assistant needs 8k context; long-form debug sessions require 32k support for a subset of users. Need dedicated instances with kernel selection tuned for long-context attention and KV cache sizing to avoid memory thrash.
- Quantization: run comparisons across fp16, int8 (GPTQ-style), and 4-bit on less-critical reranking workloads. Customer wants quantization profile recommendations per workload: keep fp16 for code-critical paths, 8-bit for embeddings and rerank to save cost. SE to supply per-model BLEU/functional test deltas.
- Batching & KV cache: prefer conservative batching for code-completions (to preserve latency), aggressive batching for embeddings. KV cache policy: sticky per-session cache with TTL and eviction tuned to average session length; Redwood's auto-prefix cache looked promising in demo.

Open negotiation items (SLA / Sizing / Commercial):
- Formal throughput guarantees: Helmstone insists on a guaranteed baseline throughput SLA (tokens/sec / concurrency) with credits for violations. Draft SLO language requested.
- Reserved GPU planning: confirm exact GPU SKU mapping (A100v4 vs A100S vs H100) and equivalence in SOW; ask for pricing delta for A100->H100 swap.
- Quantization fallback policy: need an automatic fallback path to fp16 for critical code completions if quantized model fails regression gates.

- Legal/commercial: Redwood pricing deck + draft SOW update to include SLA wording (shared via drive).
